title: Binary Tree Tilt
summary: Calculate the tilt of each node in a binary tree by finding the absolute difference between the sum of the left subtree and the sum of the right subtree.
statement: Calculate the tilt of each node in a binary tree by finding the absolute difference between the sum of the left subtree and the sum of the right subtree. Sum these tilts to get the total tilt of the tree. If a node lacks a left or right child, its subtree sum is considered zero.
constraints: A node's tilt is abs(sum of left subtree - sum of right subtree). Return the sum of tilts at every node.

hints: A parent's tilt depends on subtree sums, not child tilts.
Compute sums bottom-up and accumulate each node's absolute difference separately.
After both children, add abs(left_sum-right_sum) to the total and pass node.val+left_sum+right_sum upward.
Negative node values still participate in subtree sums before taking the absolute difference.
editorial: Process nodes after their children. Add the absolute difference of their two subtree sums to a running total, and retain the complete sum including the current value for the parent. Do not replace a subtree sum with its tilt, height, or immediate child value. An explicit postorder stack supports deep chains; consumed child sums are removed to keep auxiliary storage proportional to tree height.
